keyVerseText: And his father refused, and said, I know it, my son, I know it: he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great: but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations. multitude: Heb. fulness
rootMeaning: The root of מְלֹא (mᵉlôʼ) is מָלֵא (mâlêʼ), which conveys the idea of filling, fulfilling, or bringing to completion. This root encompasses actions like accomplishing, confirming, and satisfying, emphasizing a state of being full or complete. The literal root sense enriches the common English gloss 'full' by implying not only physical fullness but also the idea of fulfillment, completion, and abundance, highlighting both tangible and figurative dimensions of filling.
usageInScripture: The word מְלֹא appears 39 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is most frequently translated as 'full' or 'fulness,' reflecting its core meaning of that which fills or completes. It is used idiomatically to denote entire contents, a multitude, or a full measure, as seen in translations like 'and the fulness' and 'and all that is therein.' This range from literal fullness to figurative abundance or multitude reveals the word's versatility in describing both physical quantities and collective entities.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מְלֹא deepens our grasp of God's providence and the completeness of His creation and promises. The concept of fullness resonates with the biblical theme of God filling all things and fulfilling His purposes perfectly. It points to the sufficiency found in God alone and the abundance He provides, whether in blessing, judgment, or the unfolding of His covenant. This word reminds believers that God's plans are complete and that His blessings overflow beyond mere measure, reflecting His sovereign hand in history and salvation.
keyVerseReflection: In Genesis 48:19, the term translated as 'multitude' or 'fulness' underscores the promise that the younger brother's descendants will not only be numerous but will fill the earth with their presence. This fullness conveys God's blessing of multiplication and expansion, affirming His faithfulness to Abraham's covenant. The use of מְלֹא here enriches the verse by emphasizing the abundant and comprehensive nature of the promised blessing, portraying a future that is both vast and divinely ordained.
